name: milk stout braised beef
instructions:
The meat sibling of [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]] — same milk-stout dark register, applied to a beef braise. Oxtail and/or english short rib browned, then braised low with milk stout + beef broth + tomato paste + white onion + garlic + A DILL PICKLE in the pot (the anglo-dark/central-european tang kit working on meat).

SERVES 4. Dutch oven, 325°F.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- oxtail and/or english-cut short ribs (~2-3 lb)
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil (for browning)
- 1 white onion, chopped
- 3-4 cloves garlic
- 1-2 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 bottle milk stout (see MILK STOUT note)
- beef broth (enough with the stout to come partway up the meat)
- 1 DILL PICKLE (whole or halved, into the braise — see PICKLE note)
- salt and black pepper

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. PREHEAT the oven to 325°F.

2. BROWN THE BEEF: heat the vegetable oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Season the oxtail/short ribs with salt and pepper; brown well on all sides, in batches if needed. Transfer to a plate.

3. EVERYTHING IN THE POT: return the beef to the pot and add the chopped white onion, garlic, tomato paste, milk stout, beef broth, and the dill pickle. Season lightly (the pickle and broth carry salt — taste before adding much).

4. COVER AND BRAISE at 325°F for 2-3 HOURS — MAYBE LONGER FOR OXTAIL (oxtail's connective tissue takes its time; go until the meat is falling off the bone / fork-tender; short rib usually lands earlier than oxtail).

5. SERVE: over mash, with bread, or alongside [[braised-turnips]]. Skim excess fat from the surface if the braise threw a lot (oxtail especially will).
notes:
The meat expression of the milk-stout dark register — cooked as a double feature alongside [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]]'s third cook. Same structural logic: dark bitter anchor (milk stout) + warmth (tomato paste + garlic) + pickle tang.

=== THE CUTS — OXTAIL AND ENGLISH SHORT RIB ===

Both are high-connective-tissue braising cuts that melt into gelatin over the long cook:
- OXTAIL: the most gelatinous — richest finished braise, longest cook (push past 3 hours if it's not falling apart). The victorian oxtail tradition (and Nigella's milk-stout oxtail) is the precedent for exactly this cut + milk stout pairing.
- ENGLISH-CUT SHORT RIB (thick single-bone pieces): meatier, usually done sooner than oxtail. Either alone works; the mix gives you both registers in one pot.

=== MILK STOUT SPECIFICALLY — THE BITTERNESS BUDGET ===

Same rule as [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]] and Nigella's oxtail: MILK STOUT, not regular stout. Regular stout's bitterness compounds over a long reduction; milk stout's lactose sweetness keeps the braise rounded. (And no marmite here — the stout owns the dark-bitter slot; marmite and stout don't stack.)

=== THE DILL PICKLE IN THE BRAISE ===

A whole dill pickle goes INTO the pot — the anglo-dark/central-european tang kit applied to meat. It slowly gives its sourness to the braising liquid the way the pickle juice did in the lentil version, rounding the dark stout base. This is the german logic (sour into the braise — sauerbraten thinking) rather than a garnish move.

=== WANT TO TRY — PORK SHOULDER (CHEAPER) ===

Open question: would this work with PORK SHOULDER instead of the beef cuts? Much cheaper, similar braise-friendly connective tissue, and the technique is nearly identical to [[carolina-pulled-pork]]'s dutch-oven braise (which already proves pork shoulder + vinegar-tang braising liquid works — this would swap the vinegar-broth base for stout + pickle). Suspicion: yes it works, but the beef-broth backbone might want to stay beef even under pork, or swap to chicken broth per the carolina pattern. Untested.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]]: the vegetarian sibling — same register (milk stout + tomato paste + pickle tang), lentils in the meat slot. The double-feature pair.
- [[carolina-pulled-pork]]: the other dutch-oven meat braise — vinegar-broth register instead of stout; the pork-shoulder want-to-try above would bridge the two.
- [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]]: the french-register beef braise (wine kit). Same chassis, different country — see the balancer-register split documented in [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]].
- [[braised-turnips]]: natural side.
original_chef: Mine — the meat expression of the milk-stout-cottage-lentils register. Precedent: Nigella Lawson's oxtail with milk stout; victorian oxtail tradition.
